name: Czech Republic
visaRequirements: Schengen Visa required for most non-EU citizens
currency: Czech Koruna (CZK) — the Czech Republic is in the EU but not the Eurozone
bestExperience: Best experience: simply walking around Prague's old town.

about.description: Prague survived the twentieth century largely unbombed, which is why its old town still looks the way it does. The castle complex on the hill, the Charles Bridge across the Vltava, and the Old Town Square are all within walking distance of each other — compact enough that a single well-planned day covers the essentials.
highlights: Prague Castle and St. Vitus Cathedral
The Astronomical Clock on Old Town Square
Golden Lane inside the castle complex
One of the most walkable historic centres in Europe

travelTips.bestTimeToVisit: May to September for long days; December for the Christmas markets
transportation: Trams and metro cover the city cheaply
The historic centre is best done entirely on foot
Well connected by train and bus to Dresden, Vienna and Berlin
culturalNotes: The Czech Republic uses the koruna, not the euro
Avoid the currency exchange booths in the tourist centre
Check opening days before planning the castle — interiors close earlier than the grounds
